deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics. It is part of lecture notes, probably a student's or a copied course, on ancient history: the wars of the Diadochi after Alexander the Great. It continues the previous page's account of the siege of Rhodes by Demetrius Poliorcetes (305–304 BC).

Content, in order:
- Demetrius had to withdraw from Rhodes ('abziehen').
- Just then an embassy came from Greece asking him to return, because Cassander had designs on Athens.
- In 304 he drove Cassander out of the Greek cities.
- Cassander was not strong enough to resist him, so he brought about a new alliance of Lysimachus, Seleucus and Ptolemy against Antigonus (dated 302).
- Antigonus then recalled Demetrius to unite his whole force.
- Lysimachus crossed into Asia Minor ('Vorderasien').
- Cassander sent [12000?] men under Plistarch (Pleistarchus).
- Ptolemy also came, but on a false [rumour, continued on the next page] he turned back to Egypt.

The next page goes on to the battle of Ipsus (301 BC) and the start of the 'Dritter Zeitraum' (history of the Hellenistic successor kingdoms). There are no derivations, formulas or computations to reconstruct.
errors: No mathematical errors are possible, since the page contains no mathematics.

Historical framing (not a mathematical error): the anti-Antigonid coalition and the expedition of Lysimachus and Pleistarchus belong to 302 BC. The decisive battle of Ipsus was in 301 BC, consistent with the next page. The 304 date for Demetrius' Greek campaign is broadly correct (304–302 BC).

results.what: Narrative of the Diadochi wars, c. 304–301 BC (Demetrius' return to Greece, the coalition against Antigonus)
results.modern_name: Hellenistic history: the Fourth Diadoch War
results.usually_credited_to: Standard ancient-history material (Diodorus, Plutarch), as taught in early-19th-century courses

deep.surprise_reason: These are non-mathematical history lecture notes with standard textbook content. Nothing here bears on Gauss's mathematics, and the page may not even be in Gauss's own hand.
transcription_corrections: 'Cassan der' is the hyphenated name 'Cassander', split across a line break.

'ging aus [?] Asien nach Vorderasien': the word after 'aus' is unclear in the image. Historically Lysimachus crossed from Europe (Thrace) into Asia Minor, so 'aus Europa' may be intended; reading it as 'Asien' is doubtful.

'12000 [?] Mann unter Plistarch': the figure is hard to read in the image and could be 1200 or 12000. 12000 matches the ancient sources (Pleistarchus with about 12,000 foot), so 12000 is the likely reading.
'so brachte er ein neues Bündniß' appears to be written 'brachte er ein' with an inserted/overwritten 'er'. The reading in the machine transcription is acceptable.
The final word 'falsches' continues onto the next page, presumably as 'falsches Gerücht ... gemacht' ('[turned back] on a false rumour').
